Wave 1 · resolve conflict

Records

  • ADR-SAG-0004

Change

  • Resolution: reconcile.
  • Reword ADR-SAG-0004: “Crates are in four layers, and a crate depends only on crates in lower layers. Layer 1, core types and traits: `sc-agent-schema`, `sc-agent-sqlite`, `sc-agent-types`, `sc-agent-config`, `sc-agent-log`. Layer 2, one crate per API shape: `sc-decision-systemone`, `sc-anthropic`, `sc-openai`. Layer 3, shared behaviour and the API: `sc-decision-runner`, `sc-llm`. Layer 4, thin public surface: the `decidr` CLI and the Python wheel. `sitr` on `sc-treesitter` is a separate stack. Behaviour shared by crates in one layer is placed in a lower layer. A difference between them stays in the higher layer. A provider, a model and a URL are data: adding one changes configuration and no Rust code. CLI agents and SDK agents get their own crates later. Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message. A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002). An error may carry more fields. Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.” → “Crates are in four layers. A crate depends only on crates in lower layers, except within layer 1: schema, then types, then config and sqlite, then log; a layer-1 crate depends only on layer-1 crates earlier in that order. Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message. A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002). An error may carry more fields. Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.”

4. Align ADR-SAG-0019 wheel boundary with ADR-SAG-0004 (docs/sc-decision-runner/)

Wave 1 · resolve conflict

Records

  • ADR-SAG-0019

Change

  • Resolution: reconcile.
  • Reword ADR-SAG-0019: “The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3. 1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path. **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged. - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping. - model selectors are Run arguments. - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path. - Python results are typed values, not dicts. - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced. **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library. 2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.”

Rewording (rare; justified)

ADR-SAG-0019: The explicit architecture direction places the thin wheel in layer 4 and shared implementation in lower layers; the remaining decisions are retained for review.

Justification

Arch-ai directs resolving the claim that every consumer concern belongs in sc-decidr against ADR-SAG-0004 v0.5.0.

Source of truth

ANC-021 — Owner said: “You need to be able to push shared methods down and move differences up” — commit 2e54ef62

Expected improvement

Aligns the wheel boundary with the layer-4 architecture.

REQ-SAG-0501 TypeSafe API as decidr subcommands

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.0

Statements

  • `decidr` MUST expose the TypeSafe API as CLI subcommands.
  • `decidr` MUST be able to send any request the TypeSafe API accepts.

Requirement

Definitions: `decidr` is the sc-agent decision command-line tool. The TypeSafe API is the Jev decision API (`POST /v1/systemone`, `GET /v1/models`).

Rationale

Exposing the TypeSafe API as a CLI is requirement #1 for sc-agent: any Jev query can be run from the command line.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each request example in the TypeSafe API documentation (https://docs.typesafe.ai, OpenAPI 0.2.0 at https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) can be sent through a `decidr` subcommand and returns the API's response.
  • The TypeSafe models list is returned by a `decidr` subcommand.

REQ-SAG-0503 doctor warns about models missing from the catalog

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Statements

  • `decidr doctor` MUST compare each configured provider's model list with the catalog.
  • `decidr doctor` MUST warn about every model a provider lists that is in no provider table, naming the provider and the model.
  • `decidr doctor` MUST list every detected provider key in the order sc-agent would use it.
  • For each detected key, `decidr doctor` MUST show the source it came from: the environment, the repository-root `.env`, or the platform keyring.

  • When every listed model is in the catalog, `decidr doctor` prints no missing-model warning.

NFR-SAG-0001 Session logging at 40,000 sessions per task

NFR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.1

Statements

  • All sessions of one repo, agent role and project MUST be written to one session log file.
  • Session logging MUST NOT create one log file per session.

Requirement

Definitions: A task is one caller run. A session is one model request with its own ULID `session_id`; every send of that request, including busy resends, belongs to the same session. `repo` identifies the repository a session ran in. `project` is a caller-supplied project or phase name. `agent_role` is a caller-supplied name for the type of work done or the agent that did it (REQ-SAG-0004). One task of the owner's produced 40,000 sessions, each one Jev query.

Rationale

The owner analyses 10,000 to 20,000 or more decisions at a time to tune consumer code, and one task has already produced 40,000 sessions.

Acceptance criteria

A load test verifies that a task of many sessions with one repo, agent role and project writes one row per session, each with a distinct `session_id`, to one file.

NFR-SAG-0003 One Python floor for sc-agent's wheel and its consumers

NFR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.1

Statements

The sc-decidr wheel MUST declare Python 3.11 or newer.

Requirement

Definitions: - `floors.toml` is the file at the repository root that writes down the workspace's floor values for sc-compose templates to read. - The Python floor is `[python].floor` in `floors.toml`. - The abi3 feature is the `abi3-py3NN` feature of pyo3 that sets a wheel's stable-ABI tag. - The Python binding crate is `crates/sc-agent-py`, which builds the sc-decidr wheel.

Rationale

The declared Python floor and the pyo3 abi3 tag disagreed, so the wheel tag claimed support the package metadata refused. One floor value, written down in `floors.toml`, removes that mismatch and makes raising the floor a one-line change. `floors.toml` records the value; nothing in sc-agent checks it. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "No hand built checks." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

An inspection of the built sc-decidr wheel package metadata confirms it declares Python 3.11 or newer.

  • REQ-SAG-0018

NFR-SAG-0004 One owner for every piece of logic and data; everything else calls it

NFR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.0

Statements

  • Every shared fact MUST have a single owner.
  • Code that needs a shared fact MUST obtain it by calling its owner.

Requirement

Definitions: - sc-agent is this repository: its Rust crates, the sc-decidr wheel and its scripts. - A shared fact is a piece of logic or data that more than one program needs, such as the provider table, the provider-key list, the model table, the session-log layout or ULID minting. - The owner of a shared fact is the one function, constant or table that holds it.

Rationale

Two consumers each rebuilt the wheel boundary and the copies diverged (ADR-SAG-0019, Context). The first phase-j plan copied the provider-key list into four places, re-implemented the session-log layout in template Python and minted ULIDs in both Rust and Python. One owner per fact keeps one place to change and removes divergence.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test in the sc-agent Rust crate asserts that each listed shared fact (provider table, provider-key list, model table, session-log layout, ULID minting) is defined by one owner.
  • A unit test calls the sc-decidr wheel's provider-key list, session-row reader and `run_id` minting and asserts each returns the value of its owner in the sc-agent Rust crate.
  • Inspection: `rg -n` over sc-agent for the provider-key names, the session-log path layout and ULID minting, outside test fixtures, returns matches only in their owners.
  • Inspection: `rg -n` over `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2` for the provider-key names, the session-log path layout and ULID minting returns no match.
  • Inspection: `rg -n` over a consumer module rendered from `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2` for the provider-key names, the session-log path layout and ULID minting returns no match.

REQ-SAG-0001 Created ids are ULIDs

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Statements

  • Every id sc-agent generates MUST be a ULID.
  • An id whose format an external API defines MUST use that API's format, including UUID where the API defines a UUID.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT generate a UUID for an id that no external API defines.

Requirement

Definitions: An id is any identifier sc-agent generates, such as a session id or a send id. ULID is the 26-character Crockford base32 Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier. UUID means universally unique identifier. API means application programming interface.

Rationale

One sortable id format across all session logs lets rows from every crate and machine be ordered and joined without conversion.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test verifies that every id written to a session log by sc-agent parses as a ULID.
  • A workspace search finds UUID generation only at call sites that build a request for an external API that defines a UUID.

REQ-SAG-0002 Errors are a discriminated union carried from bottom to top

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.3.0

Statements

  • Every public API MUST return a discriminated union of success and error.
  • Rust APIs MUST return `Result<T, E>` from the lowest layer to the top-level CLI and PyO3 entry points.
  • An error MUST carry the error id and message of every lower-layer error that caused it.
  • A layer that changes an error MUST change it only by adding detail.
  • Error text received from a provider MUST be kept whole.
  • Exception (owner-approved): the API key MUST never appear in an error or log.
  • Every error MUST have a stable id.
  • Rust code MUST NOT panic on any input or runtime failure.
  • A layer MUST NOT drop or replace a lower-layer error id or message.

Requirement

Definitions: A discriminated union is a tagged result type whose variant names the outcome, such as Rust `Result<T, E>` with an error enum. An error id is the stable identifier of one error case. A lower layer is any crate or function an API calls.

Rationale

Agents and tools act on errors programmatically. A dropped lower-layer id or a panic removes the information needed to decide the next step. This rule applies to every repository the owner maintains. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "always return descriminated unions w/ error info"

Acceptance criteria

  • A test that injects a failure at the lowest layer of a call path receives, at the CLI and PyO3 entry points, that failure's error id and message in the returned error.
  • A test in which a provider or local runner echoes the attached key receives an error whose id is unchanged and which contains no copy of the key.
  • Clippy passes with the workspace lint configuration (`[workspace.lints.clippy]` in `Cargo.toml`), which denies panicking constructs in non-test code.

REQ-SAG-0003 Log locations and retention

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.9.0

Statements

  • With no Logger injected, each CLI MUST write its general log to `~/.sc-agent/logs/<cli>.log.jsonl`.
  • When `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` is set and non-empty, that CLI MUST use its value in place of `~/.sc-agent`.
  • When `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is set and not empty, the generated client MUST use that folder in place of `~/.sc-agent/` for its logs.
  • Session logs MUST be written under `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` (REQ-SAG-0005).
  • A session log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
  • A run log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT contain code that removes a general log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT remove a session log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT remove a run log.

Requirement

Definitions: sc-agent is the crates and CLIs of this repository. A CLI is one of the command-line programs decidr or sitr; `<cli>` is its name in lower case and `<CLI>` in upper case. A Logger is an sc-observability logger that a caller passes to a CLI's library entry point. The general log is the diagnostic log of one entry point (ADR-SAG-0021); decidr's is `decidr.log.jsonl` and sitr's is `sitr.log.jsonl`. A session log is the record of every session; a session is one model request with its own ULID `session_id`, and every send of that request, including busy resends, belongs to it. A link record ties one run to one session (REQ-SAG-0005). A run log is the file of link records that sits beside a session log in the same directory. To remove a log is to rotate, prune or delete it. The generated client is the Python module a consumer renders from the sc-decidr wheel's sc-compose template (REQ-SAG-0018). The client name is the consumer's product name, a constant in the generated client, and equals its `agent_role` (REQ-SAG-0004), such as `plan-anchor` or `judge-jev`. The client Logger is the Logger the generated client obtains from the wheel under the client name (REQ-SAG-0008). `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is the environment variable named by the client name uppercased with hyphens replaced by underscores. The default session files are the session files REQ-SAG-0005 names for an agent role. The client's logs are the general log the client Logger writes and the default session files.

Rationale

Session logs are the long-term record used to analyse tens of thousands of decisions, so losing any of them loses data. Link records are append-only and immutable, so the run log is kept the same way.

Acceptance criteria

  • A CLI run of decidr with nothing configured writes `~/.sc-agent/logs/decidr.log.jsonl`.
  • A CLI run of sitr with nothing configured writes `~/.sc-agent/logs/sitr.log.jsonl`.
  • A CLI run of decidr with `DECIDR_LOG_ROOT` set to `<dir>` writes `<dir>/logs/decidr.log.jsonl`.
  • A CLI run of decidr with `DECIDR_LOG_ROOT` set to `<dir>` writes its session log under `<dir>/sessions/`.
  • A unit test sets `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` to a test folder, makes one sc-decidr call, and finds the general log and session rows under that folder and nothing under `~/.sc-agent/`.
  • A CLI run of decidr with nothing configured writes its session log under `~/.sc-agent/sessions/`.
  • A Rust unit test shows a session log older than the sc-observability retention age is still present after a new session.
  • A Rust unit test shows a run log older than the sc-observability retention age is still present after a new session.
  • Inspection of `rg -n 'rotat|prune|retention' crates/` shows no code that removes a general log.
  • A Rust unit test shows a session log is unchanged and present after decidr runs a new session.
  • A Rust unit test shows a run log's earlier lines are unchanged after decidr runs a new session.
  • A Rust unit test shows a session log past the sc-observability rotation size has no rotated copy after a new session.
  • A Rust unit test shows a run log past the sc-observability rotation size has no rotated copy after a new session.

Related

  • ADR-SAG-0002
  • ADR-SAG-0021
  • REQ-SAG-0005

REQ-SAG-0004 Session log identity: repo, agent role, project and tool

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Statements

  • Every session row MUST carry its identity.
  • sc-agent MUST refuse every query whose identity is not valid.
  • In a git repository, a query's repository MUST be that repository's origin name.
  • Outside a git repository, a query's repository MUST be `local/<host>/<folder-name>`.
  • A query's project MUST be the project that REQ-SAG-0021 resolves for it.
  • The `decidr` CLI MUST accept an agent role from its user.
  • The Python bindings of sc-agent MUST accept an agent role from their caller.
  • A generated consumer client MUST set the agent role to the client's product name.
  • A generated consumer client MUST NOT let its user set the agent role.

Requirement

Definitions: sc-agent is the Rust core that sends decision requests and writes session logs. A session row is a row of a session log (REQ-SAG-0005). A query's identity is the repository it ran in, its project (REQ-SAG-0021), its agent role, and the name and released version of the program that sent it (ADR-SAG-0021, Session identity). A session row's identity is its `session_id`, which identifies the session, and the identity of the query it records. An identity is valid when every part is present and the project and agent role are slugs. A git repository's origin name is `<host>/<owner>/<repo>` taken from its `origin` URL, with no URL scheme and no `.git` suffix. An agent role is the agent or app making the request (ADR-SAG-0021). A generated consumer client is the Python module a consumer renders from the sc-decidr wheel's template, and its product name is the client-name constant it carries, such as `plan-anchor`. In `local/<host>/<folder-name>`, `<host>` is the output of `hostname` and `<folder-name>` is the name of the working directory. A slug is lowercase text using only `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`. To refuse a query is to return an error for it without making a model call or writing a session row.

Rationale

Session logs are separated and analysed by repository, by type of work and by project or phase, and each row traces back to the program and version that sent it. Who sets each part, and where a refusal is raised, is carried by ADR-SAG-0021 (Session identity) and ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unit test: a written session row carries `session_id`, repository, project, agent role, program name and program version.
  • Unit test: a query with a missing part or a non-slug project or agent role returns an error, makes no model call and writes no row.
  • Unit test: origin `https://github.com/randlee/sc-agent.git` gives repository `github.com/randlee/sc-agent`.
  • Unit test: folder `work` on host `m5` outside git gives repository `local/m5/work`.
  • Unit test of project resolution: the project a row carries is the one REQ-SAG-0021 resolves.
  • CLI run: `decidr send --agent-role sanity` writes a row with agent role `sanity`.
  • Unit test: a Python bindings call with agent role `sanity` writes a row with that agent role.
  • Unit test of the generated plan-anchor client: its rows carry agent role `plan-anchor`.

REQ-SAG-0005 Session log rows and run links

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.8.2

Statements

  • Session logs MUST be written as JSONL.
  • For every query whose model call succeeded, sc-agent MUST append a session row to the query's session log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT append more than one session row for one query.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT append a session row for a failed call; the error goes to the general log.

Requirement

Definitions: JSON is JavaScript Object Notation (RFC 8259). JSONL is newline-delimited JSON: one JSON object per line. A query is one decision request sent through `send`, or one request of a `send_batch` call. A query's session log is the JSONL file `sessions.jsonl`, and its run log is the JSONL file `runs.jsonl` in the same directory. A session row is the one line of a session log that records one query whose model call succeeded and its result. A failed call is one that ends in an error (auth, busy, quota, network or cancel). A Run is the context object through which every query is sent (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). A link record is the one line of a run log that ties a Run to the session row that answered one of its queries.

Rationale

Every successfully answered query from every tool lands in the session log, while errors go to the general log, so a tool references a row by `session_id` instead of copying the query or the response. The run log records which Run each row answered, because one row can answer many Runs through cache hits. What a row and a link record hold, and that both logs are never rotated or pruned, is in ADR-SAG-0021 (Session log).

Acceptance criteria

  • Every line of the `sessions.jsonl` that three sends write parses as one JSON object.
  • Three sends with `repo` `github.com/randlee/sc-agent`, `agent_role` `rust-developer` and `project` `phase-b` add three rows to one `sessions.jsonl`.
  • One Python `sc_agent.send` adds one row to a `sessions.jsonl` under `<log_root>/sessions/`.
  • A `decidr` CLI send with `repo` `github.com/randlee/sc-agent`, `agent_role` `rust-developer` and `project` `phase-b` adds one row to `sessions.jsonl`.
  • A query sent four times after three busy responses adds one row.
  • A send that fails with a 401 adds no row to `sessions.jsonl`.
  • A batch of 3 through a Run adds 3 link records to `runs.jsonl` in the same directory.

REQ-SAG-0007 Return values are not rounded

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.3.2

Statements

  • sc-agent MUST NOT round a returned float.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT convert a returned float to an integer type.

Requirement

Definitions: A returned float is any floating-point value sc-agent returns, such as a Jev probability, confidence or score.

Rationale

This requirement stops an implementation from rounding or casting a value and so hiding information from the end user. Rounding is the consumer's concern: a value rounded inside sc-agent loses information no consumer can recover. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "I would never create a requirement requiring subnanosecond rounding for a http call." "Don't round % to int."

Acceptance criteria

  • Rust API: a unit test sends a request whose Jev probability is 0.123456789 to a stub server and asserts `send` returns 0.123456789 exactly.
  • CLI: a CLI run of `decidr send` against a stub server whose Jev probability is 0.123456789 prints 0.123456789 exactly in its JSON output.
  • Python bindings: a Python test calls `send` against a stub server whose Jev probability is 0.123456789 and asserts the returned value is 0.123456789 exactly.
  • Inspection: `rg -n 'f32|Decimal|i64' crates/sc-agent/src` shows no fractional decision value held in a type other than `f64`.
  • A unit test passes a Jev confidence of 0.875 through sc-agent and asserts the returned value is 0.875, not 1 or 0.88.
  • Inspection: `rg -n 'round' crates/` finds no rounding of a returned decision value.

REQ-SAG-0008 Logger injection into the Rust API and the wheel

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Statements

  • The Rust API MUST accept an injected general Logger.
  • When a Python caller requests a named Logger, the wheel MUST return a Logger built from the linked crate.
  • The wheel MUST NOT depend on the `sc-observability` Python package.

Requirement

Definitions: A Logger is an sc-observability crate `Logger`. The linked crate is the sc-observability Rust crate compiled into the wheel. The general logger writes the general log. Injecting a Logger means the caller passes in the Logger sc-agent uses. The wheel is the sc-decidr Python package, which holds the decidr and sitr Python APIs (ADR-SAG-0021).

Rationale

The wheel already links the sc-observability crate, so it hands that crate's Logger to Python and receives the same object back: one Logger, one queue, no bridge.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unit test: a Rust caller injects a general Logger with a test sink and finds every general-log record of the call in that sink.
  • Python test: a program obtains a Logger named `t` from the wheel, writes one record, and finds its record in `~/.sc-agent/logs/t.log.jsonl`.
  • Install check: in a fresh virtual environment, `pip install sc-decidr` installs no `sc-observability` package.

REQ-SAG-0010 No sleep()

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.1

Statements

The source code of this project MUST NOT call any sleep function.

Requirement

`sc-agent` is this project. A sleep function includes `std::thread::sleep`, `std::thread::sleep_until` and `tokio::time::sleep`.

Rationale

A sleeping thread cannot react to cancellation or new work; waits are made on events or deadlines that cancellation can end. This requirement is met by a timed wait that cancellation can end, such as a wait on a channel or condition variable. It does not require a clock abstraction or an injected time source. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "No sleep (is async requirement)."

Acceptance criteria

A workspace search of non-test source finds no call to a sleep function.

REQ-SAG-0011 Interrupt cancels cleanly

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.0

Statements

  • When `decidr` receives an interrupt, it MUST cancel the batch.
  • When a `KeyboardInterrupt` is raised in `sc-agent-py`, it MUST cancel the batch.
  • After an interrupt, every unfinished request MUST end with `decision.cancelled`.
  • The session log MUST hold the row of every request that finished before the interrupt when `decidr` exits or the Python call returns.
  • A `KeyboardInterrupt` in `sc-agent-py` MUST be caught inside the Python call.
  • After a `KeyboardInterrupt`, the Python call MUST return one result per request of the batch.
  • `decidr` MUST exit non-zero after an interrupt.

Requirement

Definitions: `decidr` is the decision CLI, and `sc-agent-py` is the Python wheel that holds the decidr API. An interrupt is Ctrl-C, SIGINT or SIGTERM delivered to `decidr`, or a `KeyboardInterrupt` raised in Python while `sc-agent-py` is running. The session log is the JSONL file `sessions.jsonl` that holds one row for each request sent to a model (REQ-SAG-0005). A batch is the set of requests sent by one `decidr` command or one `sc-agent-py` call. The Python call is the `sc-agent-py` call that sent the batch. An unfinished request is a request of the batch that has no result when the interrupt arrives. `decision.cancelled` is the error id given to a cancelled request.

Rationale

An interrupted batch must leave a complete, readable session log and a clear failure status instead of lost rows and a silent exit.

Acceptance criteria

  • CLI run: sending SIGINT to `decidr` during a batch stops the in-flight requests.
  • CLI run: sending SIGTERM to `decidr` during a batch stops the in-flight requests.
  • CLI run: after SIGINT, and in a separate run after SIGTERM, during a batch, every unfinished request in the output ends with `decision.cancelled`.
  • CLI run: after SIGINT, and in a separate run after SIGTERM, during a batch, the session log holds a row for every request that finished before the signal.
  • Unit test: raising `KeyboardInterrupt` during an `sc-agent-py` batch stops the in-flight requests.
  • Unit test: raising `KeyboardInterrupt` during an `sc-agent-py` batch does not raise out of the call.
  • Unit test: after `KeyboardInterrupt` during an `sc-agent-py` batch, the session log holds a row for every request that finished before the interrupt.
  • Unit test: after `KeyboardInterrupt` during an `sc-agent-py` batch, the call returns one result per request, each unfinished one a `decision.cancelled` error value.
  • CLI run: `decidr` exits non-zero after SIGINT, and in a separate run after SIGTERM, during a batch.

REQ-SAG-0016 Error values carry the send count and category as typed fields

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.9.1

Statements

  • An error value MUST have the typed fields that apply to it.
  • A typed field that is not set MUST be omitted from serialized JSON.
  • Every busy error MUST carry its number of sends in `attempts`.
  • If a request fails, the `sc-decidr` Python wheel MUST return an error value carrying the typed fields.
  • An exception raised in Python while a wheel call runs MUST be caught.
  • An exception raised in Python while a wheel call runs MUST be returned as an error value.
  • For a failed request, the `sc-decidr` Python wheel MUST NOT raise an exception.
  • A consumer MUST NOT need to parse message text to obtain a send count.
  • A consumer MUST NOT need to parse message text to obtain an error category.

Requirement

Definitions: - The `sc-decidr` Python wheel contains the decidr and sitr Python APIs (REQ-SAG-0018). - A busy error has the category `busy` (REQ-SAG-0017). - A Python exception raised while a wheel call runs includes an exception raised by a caller's `on_result` callback. - An error value is the `error` object that the CLI, the Python binding, session rows and result lines carry. It has at least an `id`, a `message` and an `action`, and may carry more fields. - The typed fields of an error value are: - `category`, the error category that REQ-SAG-0017 assigns, always set; - `attempts`, the sends made with the first included, set when the error follows a send.

Rationale

Consumers decide whether to resubmit from the category and the send count. Without typed fields these values exist only in English message text. The 0.1.0 error-JSON compatibility rule is withdrawn (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "We are still using python, schema isn't locked yet. I haven't mentioned locking schema yet. I have tools to do this that aren't on this repo. No hand built checks." Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: nothing raises; throwing exceptions is prohibited on the repo. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "Python exceptions need to be caught (return error) so app doesn't crash." Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "I would never create a requirement requiring subnanosecond rounding for a http call." "Use time structs for time." "always return descriminated unions w/ error info" Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Extra fields are fine, make sure adr doesn't limit too much. I don't want findings for returning more."

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test verifies that a busy error read in Rust and in Python, through the returned error value or the result line's `error`, carries the send count.
  • A unit test verifies that each error value reports its own `category`.
  • A unit test verifies that `decision.cancelled` carries `attempts` equal to its sends.

REQ-SAG-0017 Every error has a stable id and a stored category, and busy and network errors are retryable

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.2

Statements

  • Busy errors MUST say they are worth retrying later.
  • Network errors MUST say they are worth retrying later.
  • Every error value MUST store its category.

Requirement

Definitions: - A busy error and a network error are errors in the `busy` and `network` categories, respectively. The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. - Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out. It is not a signal for an immediate retry loop.

Rationale

Consumers that branch on error ids pin their own lists and add fallbacks today. A category stored when the error is built removes both problems without a lookup. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "always return descriminated unions w/ error info" "No hand built checks." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

REQ-SAG-0018 Python consumers integrate through one generated module rendered from a template shipped in the sc-decidr wheel

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 1.8.0

Statements

  • Every consumer MUST make its decision calls from code in its consumer module.
  • The consumer module MUST pass the model selector through unchanged.
  • The sc-decidr wheel's package data MUST include the consumer template.
  • The consumer module MUST cancel its running Run on `KeyboardInterrupt`.
  • The consent gate MUST ask for consent only when the Run's provider is TypeSafe.
  • The consumer module MUST NOT contain consumer logic.

Requirement

Definitions (how the template is built: ADR-SAG-0019 decision 1): - A consumer is a Python tool that makes Jev decision calls through the sc-decidr wheel; plan-anchor and judge-jev are the first two. - The consumer template is `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`. A consumer module is the Python file a consumer renders from it. - The sc-decidr wheel is the Python wheel that ships the `sc_agent` package. - Prompt authoring is building the text sent to the model. Result processing is handling the returned results and decision trees. Consumer logic is prompt authoring together with result processing. - A decision call is a Run's `send` or `send_batch`. - The consent gate is the consumer module's `allow_remote_judge` check before a decision call.

Rationale

The owner requires every Python consumer to integrate identically, for errors, API keys, model selection, logging and session logging, and to differ only in prompt authoring and in processing results and decision trees. A hand-copied recipe already diverged between two consumers (ADR-SAG-0019, Context); one shipped template removes that divergence. Shipping the template in the wheel makes its version the installed wheel's version.

  • A unit test scans plan-anchor and judge-jev and finds every decision call inside a module rendered from the consumer template.
  • A loopback unit test passes `haiku` to each rendered module and finds `haiku` as the model selector of its decision call.
  • A unit test finds the consumer template in the built wheel's package data.
  • A loopback test raises `KeyboardInterrupt` during a batch and finds the Run cancelled.
  • A loopback test finds consent asked for a TypeSafe Run and not asked for a `haiku` Run.
  • Inspection of `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2` finds no prompt text or result handling.

REQ-SAG-0702 A Run may override the send timeout and the worker count for its own calls only

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.7.0

Statements

  • A Run MUST accept an optional send timeout.
  • A Run MUST accept an optional worker count.
  • A Run's `timeout_secs` MUST replace the 120 s default send timeout for that Run.
  • When a Run has an override, every call through that Run MUST use the override in place of the configured value.
  • When a Run has no override, every call through that Run MUST use the configured value.
  • When a Run is given an invalid send timeout, it MUST return an error.
  • When a Run is given an invalid worker count, it MUST return an error.
  • When a provider rejects a request as too large for the model's context, the call MUST return the provider's error.
  • A Run MUST NOT clamp an override.
  • An override MUST NOT change the configuration.
  • A single call through a Run MUST NOT accept an override.

Requirement

Definitions: - The send timeout is the deadline for one HTTP send of a decision request: connect, headers and body. - The worker count is the number of requests of one batch that are sent at the same time. - A Run is the run context a tool creates, uses for its calls and then disposes. `decidr send` creates one Run per command from its `--timeout-secs` and `--workers` options. - An override is a send timeout or a worker count given to a Run. - To clamp a value is to replace it with the nearest bound of a range when it falls outside that range. - An invalid send timeout is a send timeout that is negative or not a number. - An invalid worker count is a worker count below 1. - The configured send timeout is 120 s unless configuration sets another value. - A model's context is the largest request, in tokens, that the model accepts. - The provider's error is the error value `decision.api_status` whose message is the provider's reply text.

Rationale

Different callers in one process need different parallelism and different patience. Without overrides both are fixed by configuration, so consumers refuse or ignore their own flags. The selected model's context is the only size rule for a request. Values that do not vary between the calls of one command are set once on the Run, so an override cannot leak into another Run. Error values rather than exceptions keep every Python result typed.

Acceptance criteria

  • A Rust unit test builds a Run with a 10 s send timeout and checks the transport timeout is 10 s.
  • A Rust unit test builds a Run with `timeout_secs` of 30 s and checks its sends use 30 s, not 120 s.
  • A Rust unit test builds a Run with a worker count of 2 and checks the batch runs 2 workers.
  • A Rust unit test runs `decidr send --timeout-secs 10 --batch --workers 2` and checks the Run's send timeout is 10 s and its worker count is 2.
  • A Rust unit test builds a Run with no override after one with overrides and checks it uses the configured send timeout and worker count.
  • A Rust unit test gives a Run a negative send timeout and checks the result is an error value.
  • A Rust unit test gives a Run a NaN send timeout and checks the result is an error value.
  • A Rust unit test gives a Run a worker count of 0 and checks the result is an error value.
  • A Rust unit test gives a Run a worker count of -1 and checks the result is an error value.
  • A Python unit test builds `sc_agent.Run` with `timeout_secs` and `workers` and checks a batch through it uses both values.
  • A Python unit test checks that `run.send` and `run.send_batch` have no `timeout_secs` or `workers` parameter.
  • A Rust unit test has a provider reject a request as too large for the model's context and checks the call returns the provider's error.
  • A Rust unit test gives a Run a worker count above the configured one and checks that many workers run.
  • A Rust unit test checks the configuration is unchanged after a Run with overrides.
  • A Rust unit test checks that the per-call send and batch signatures have no override parameter.

REQ-SAG-0013 Config bounds

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.3.0

Statements

  • The value of `workers` MUST be a positive count.
  • Timeouts MUST be represented as `Duration` values.
  • An invalid setting value MUST result in an error.
  • An error for an invalid setting value MUST identify the configuration setting with the invalid value.
  • A request to a plain-http endpoint on a non-loopback host MUST NOT carry a key.

Requirement

Definitions: `workers` is the configuration setting for the worker count used to fan out a batch. Timeouts are time limits for operations, including individual requests. A `Duration` is a span of time represented by a time struct. A configuration setting is a named setting supplied by configuration, such as `workers`. An invalid setting value is a value that violates the applicable rules for the setting, such as `workers = 0`. A key is a secret used to authenticate a request. A positive count is a whole-number count greater than zero. Plain-http describes an endpoint using the `http` URL scheme. A loopback host is named or addressed through the requesting machine’s loopback interface.

Rationale

Detecting an invalid configuration value at load time tells the operator which setting to fix and avoids a mid-batch failure. Refusing keys on plain-http requests to non-loopback hosts prevents credentials from being sent in clear text. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Use time structs for time." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • Loading `workers = 0` fails with an error that identifies `workers`.
  • A request to a plain-http endpoint on a non-loopback host carries no key.

REQ-SAG-0019 Configuration file locations and lookup order

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.8.0

Statements

  • When a required setting has no built-in default and no layer sets it, the CLI MUST return a missing-setting error.
  • Each configuration file MUST accept the shared settings.
  • A CLI file MUST accept that CLI's settings.
  • An unknown key in a configuration file MUST cause a typed load error.
  • The `cache` setting MUST default to `true`.
  • A model entry MUST add one row to the model table.
  • A model entry MUST override the model its name selects.
  • A local endpoint's address MUST be settable in configuration.
  • When the CLI does not run inside a git work tree, it MUST skip the local-folder layers.
  • Each CLI's `<cli> doctor` command, such as `decidr doctor`, MUST report the settings table.
  • In each row of the settings table, the `source` cell MUST show the source of that row's value.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST report the path of every file in the nine layers.
  • For each file in the nine layers, `<cli> doctor` MUST report whether it exists.
  • When a CLI fails to load a configuration file, its error MUST name the failure location.
  • A CLI MUST NOT read another CLI's `<cli>.json`.
  • While it loads configuration, a CLI MUST NOT write to any configuration file.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST NOT send a model request.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST NOT write a file.
  • Configuration MUST NOT change a paid API's base address.

Requirement

Definitions: A CLI is an sc-agent command-line program that reads configuration, such as `decidr`; `<cli>` is its program name. `sitr` reads no configuration. The shared file is `sc-agent.json`. A CLI file is `<cli>.json` or its optional override file `<cli>.local.json`. The global folder is `~/.sc-agent/`, the user's home directory joined with `.sc-agent` on every platform, relocated to the folder named by `SC_AGENT_HOME` when that variable is nonempty. An explicit `--config-dir` (or wheel `config_dir`) takes precedence over that variable. `<worktree>` is the root of the git work tree containing the folder the CLI runs in. The local folder is `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/`. A layer is one source of a setting's value. The local-folder layers are layers 3, 4 and 5. A typed error is an error value (REQ-SAG-0016). The key path is the dotted path of a configuration key within its file, such as `laya.port`. The shared settings are the defaults for configuration-reading CLIs that `sc-agent.json` holds. A model request is a request that asks a model for a reply, as `decidr send` does. The settings table has one row per setting and the columns `path`, `value` and `source`. The source of a value is the layer it comes from, shown as the flag, the environment variable name, the file path or `default`. A missing-setting error is a typed error that names the setting and every layer that can set it. A local endpoint is a keyless provider that runs a local model, such as laya and decider; its address is its host and port. A paid API is a remote model provider that requires an API key; its key is sent only to that provider's built-in base address. The failure location of a load error is the file path and the key path. A model entry is the configuration object `models.<alias>`; it adds a model row named `<alias>`.

Rationale

One file per CLI lets a CLI be added without changing another CLI's file. The shared file holds shared defaults that a CLI file may override. The local folder lets worktrees of one repository hold different settings, such as different phases, and keeps sc files under `.sc/`. A settable local endpoint host lets a local model run on another computer. Configuration may add model rows because built-in rows go stale; it may not redirect a paid API's key. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • CLI run (`decidr doctor`): with `SC_AGENT_HOME` set, global files are read from that folder and doctor reports those paths; an explicit configuration directory overrides it.
  • CLI run (`decidr doctor`): with `workers` set to 4 in the global `decidr.json` and 2 in the local `decidr.json`, decidr uses 2 and reports the local `decidr.json` as its source.
  • Unit test (shared settings): with `project` set only in the global `sc-agent.json`, decidr uses it.
  • Unit test (missing setting): with a required setting set in no layer, the load fails with a missing-setting error.
  • Unit test (CLI file): a `decidr` setting in `decidr.local.json` is accepted.
  • Unit test (unknown key): an unknown key in the local `decidr.json` fails the load with a typed error naming that file and key path.
  • Unit test (work tree): outside a git work tree, a `.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json` in the current folder is not read.
  • CLI run (`decidr doctor`): with `"project": "phase-a"` in `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json`, `decidr doctor` reports the row `project | phase-a | <worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json`.
  • CLI run (`decidr doctor`): with `"project": "phase-a"` only in the local `sc-agent.json`, `decidr doctor` reports the `project` row with that file as its source.
  • CLI run (`decidr doctor`): doctor lists the path of each of the nine layers' files and whether each exists.
  • Unit test (load error): a malformed local `decidr.json` fails the load with an error naming that file.
  • Unit test (other CLI): a key in a `sitr.json` beside `decidr.json` does not reach decidr's settings.
  • Unit test (no write): loading configuration leaves every configuration file's bytes and modification time unchanged.
  • Unit test (doctor offline): `decidr doctor` run through its Rust entry point with a provider stub that fails on any request completes without calling the stub.
  • Unit test (doctor no write): `decidr doctor` run in an empty temporary home and work tree leaves both directory listings unchanged.
  • Unit test (model entry): with `"models": {"luna": {"provider": "nous", "id": "openai/gpt-6.1-luna", "released": "2026-11-20"}}` in the global `sc-agent.json`, the model table has a `luna` row with id `openai/gpt-6.1-luna` and provider `nous`.
  • Unit test (paid API base address): a model entry whose `provider` is not a built-in provider fails the load with a typed error.
  • Unit test (local endpoint): with `laya.host` set to another computer's address in the global `sc-agent.json`, the resolved laya endpoint uses that host.
  • Unit test (cache default): with no `cache` set in any layer, the resolved `cache` setting is `true`.

REQ-SAG-0020 Configuration environment variable names

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.7.0

Statements

  • When a CLI loads configuration, a value set by an environment variable MUST pass the same validation as the same value set in a configuration file.
  • When an environment value fails validation, the error MUST include the name of the environment variable that set the value.
  • When an environment value is valid JSON, it MUST be parsed as JSON.
  • When an environment value is not valid JSON, it MUST be taken as a string.
  • A CLI MUST NOT read a setting from another CLI's prefix.

Requirement

Definitions: A CLI is one of sc-agent's command-line programs that reads configuration, such as `decidr`.

Rationale

A per-CLI prefix keeps an override meant for one CLI from changing another. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • With `DECIDR_LOG_ROOT=/tmp/x` set, `decidr doctor` reports the fixed log root as the value `log_root: "/tmp/x"`, separately from configuration settings (ADR-SAG-0021).
  • With `DECIDR_WORKERS=0` set, decidr exits with an error naming `DECIDR_WORKERS`, and with `"workers": 0` in the local `decidr.json` it exits with the same check's error naming that file and `workers`.
  • A unit test sets `DECIDR_LAYA__HOST=1` and checks the load fails the string host validation, and sets `DECIDR_LAYA__HOST="h"` and checks the host is `h`.
  • A unit test sets `workers` under another CLI's prefix and checks decidr's loaded `workers` keeps its default.

REQ-SAG-0021 The project/phase setting is required and shared

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.3.0

Statements

  • The `project` setting MUST be resolved through every project layer.
  • The PyO3 bindings MUST take `project` from the first project layer that sets it.
  • In the PyO3 bindings, a `project` argument MUST take the place of the `--project` flag layer.
  • A session with no project/phase MUST be refused with an error.
  • When no project layer sets `project`, a session write MUST NOT send a session.
  • When no project layer sets `project`, a session write MUST NOT write a session.
  • `project` MUST NOT have a built-in default.

Requirement

Definitions: The project/phase is the name of the project or phase a session belongs to, a block of time related to major changes. Its setting is named `project`. The layers are those of REQ-SAG-0019. The project layers are the layers of REQ-SAG-0019 that can set `project`. The PyO3 bindings are the `sc_agent` Python module of `sc-agent-py`. A typed error is an error value (REQ-SAG-0016). A session write is a call that would write a session. A built-in default is the value that layer 7 of REQ-SAG-0019 gives a setting that no other layer sets.

Rationale

Agents work by phase, so sessions are grouped by project/phase. A default would merge sessions of different phases into one file. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • With `"project": "phase-c"` in the global `sc-agent.json` and nothing else, decidr sessions are filed under project `phase-c`.
  • With `SC_PROJECT=phase-d` and `"project": "phase-c"` in the local `sc-agent.json`, sessions are filed under `phase-d`.
  • With `--project phase-e`, sessions are filed under `phase-e` whatever the environment and files set.
  • With no layer setting it, a decidr request fails with the typed error, nothing is sent, and no session row is written.

REQ-SAG-0601 Busy resend and holdoff

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Statements

  • A request that receives a busy response MUST be resent unchanged.
  • A request whose send has a network failure MUST be resent unchanged, counting toward the same maximum number of sends.
  • The maximum number of sends per request MUST be a configurable maximum, 5 by default.
  • When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.
  • Every later send to the provider endpoint MUST wait until the endpoint's not-before time.
  • When the provider gives a `Retry-After`, it MUST set the holdoff.
  • When the provider gives no `Retry-After`, the holdoffs MUST back off exponentially; this requirement does not fix their values.
  • A held-off request MUST wait in the queue until its holdoff ends, and the wait MUST end at once when the request is cancelled.
  • When sends run out on busy replies, the error MUST say busy, with the send count.
  • Authentication (401) and quota MUST NOT be resent; they MUST be returned with the remote error id and message.

Requirement

Definitions: A busy response is a non-quota HTTP 429, 502 or 529. A send is one transmission of a request; all sends of one request belong to one session. The holdoff is the time a busy request waits before it is resent. `Retry-After` is the HTTP response header that gives that time in seconds. A provider endpoint is one host reached through one `HttpClient`. The not-before time is the earliest moment a send to that endpoint may start.

Rationale

Providers signal overload with busy responses and expect clients to back off. Holding off in the queue keeps workers free and lets cancellation take effect immediately. A busy provider is busy for every worker; one worker's holdoff that the others ignore only multiplies the busy replies. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "I did ask for exponential backoff / retry when busy (i.e. 1,2,4,8,..). Nothing precise or fancy." "1,2,4,8 is an example of exp backoff not something to hard code." Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Use time structs for time." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A request answered busy every time is sent 5 times and ends with a busy error carrying a send count of 5.
  • A busy response with `Retry-After: 3` holds the request off 3 seconds; with no `Retry-After`, each holdoff is longer than the one before.
  • Cancelling a held-off request ends its wait at once and returns a cancelled result.
  • A send that times out is resent unchanged and counts toward the maximum number of sends, and a request whose last attempt timed out ends with the timeout error.
  • A 402 response is returned after one send with the remote error id and message.
  • After one worker receives a busy reply, a send from another worker to the same host through the same `HttpClient` does not start before the not-before time.
  • A send to a different host through the same `HttpClient` is not delayed by that not-before time.

Related

REQ-SAG-0602 Quota exhaustion is not busy

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.0

Statements

  • A busy status whose body marks quota exhaustion MUST be returned at once as the error `http.quota_exhausted`.
  • A 429 with a body that does not mark quota exhaustion MUST be treated as busy.
  • A quota-exhausted response MUST NOT be resent.

Requirement

Definitions: Quota exhaustion is a response whose body says the account's quota, credit or spend limit is used up, in the documented Anthropic and OpenAI shapes.

Rationale

Resending cannot succeed until the account is topped up, so holding off only delays the error. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A 429 carrying the documented Anthropic quota-exhausted body returns `http.quota_exhausted` after one send.
  • A 429 with an unrecognized body is resent under REQ-SAG-0601.

REQ-SAG-0601

REQ-SAG-0401 Credential resolution order and keyring defaults

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Statements

  • `sc-agent` MUST resolve a key from the sources in the resolution order.
  • `sc-agent` MUST use the credential from the first source in the resolution order in which the credential is present.
  • The keyring service MUST be that provider's credential-variable name.
  • The keyring account MUST be the current OS account.

Requirement

Definitions: A *provider* is an endpoint that serves a model; a provider that names a credential-variable name has a key that `sc-agent` resolves, and a keyless provider (a local model) has none. A *credential* is the API key for one provider. A *credential-variable name* is the name of the environment variable that holds a provider's credential. The *keyring service* and the *keyring account* are the two components that identify a provider's entry in the platform keyring. The *resolution order* is the process environment, then the repository-root `.env` file, then the platform keyring (the OS credential store: Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, Secret Service on Linux). A credential is *present* in a source when the source holds a value under the provider's credential-variable name; a blank platform-keyring value counts as absent. The *current OS account* is the user name of the operating-system user running the process.

Rationale

Credential handling stays in one place, so redaction and key lookup cannot disagree about which variables hold secrets. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "Keyring is super basic." Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "Isn't ENV > .env > keyring (or win/linux equivalent) standard order?" A variable already set in the environment wins over `.env`, which is also dotenvy's default. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Keyring is super basic." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

With a valid key in the environment, a different valid key in the repository-root `.env` and another in the keyring, the environment key is used; with none in the environment, the `.env` key is used; with neither, the keyring key is used.

REQ-SAG-0101 Model short names

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.0

Statements

  • Each cloud short name MUST resolve to a model in the `sc-agent` model table.
  • Each local short name MUST resolve to a local model in the model table.

Requirement

Definitions: A short name is a model name without a version. The cloud short names are `jev`, `haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`, `fable`, `luna`, `terra`, `sol` and `astra`. The local short names are `laya` and `decider`. A local model is a row whose provider is an endpoint on a computer the user runs.

Rationale

sc-agent launches any model, not only decision models, and callers select models by short name. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test resolves each cloud short name to a model in the model table.
  • A unit test resolves each local short name to a local model in the model table.

REQ-SAG-0102

REQ-SAG-0102 Model catalog: built-in and configured model rows

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.9.0

Statements

  • The built-in rows of the model table MUST be sorted by release date, newest first.
  • A short name MUST resolve to its newest row in the model table, unless a configured model entry for that name overrides it (REQ-SAG-0019).
  • A full model id MUST select its row exactly.
  • Each built-in model MUST carry the model's published release date.
  • `sc-agent` MUST NOT branch on a catalog name.

Requirement

Definitions: `sc-agent` is the program this record governs. The model table is the list of models built into `sc-agent`, together with the rows configuration adds. Each row has a short name, a fixed model id, a release date and a provider. A built-in model is a row built into `sc-agent`, not added by configuration. A full model id is a row's fixed model id, such as `claude-haiku-5-5`. A model's published release date is the date its maker announced the model as available. A catalog name is a provider name, a short name or a model id. To branch on a catalog name is to compare it with a string literal to choose what the code does.

Rationale

When a new model is released, short names such as `haiku`, `luna`, `opus` and `sol` must launch it immediately. Hard-coded rows go stale quickly, so configuration can add rows, and a configured row wins its short name (owner ruling 2026-11-25). When several providers serve the newest row, REQ-SAG-0103 orders them. Provider and model are values carried in typed data, not names to branch on. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test verifies that, with a configuration row added, the built-in rows are sorted by release date, newest first, and the configuration row is selected for its short name.
  • A unit test verifies that, of two rows sharing a short name, the short name resolves to the row with the later release date.
  • A unit test verifies that selecting a built-in row's full model id returns that row.
  • A unit test verifies that every built-in row has a release date.
  • A search of `crates/sc-agent/src` finds no comparison of a catalog name with a string literal outside the model and provider tables.

REQ-SAG-0103 Provider and model are separate

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.0

Statements

  • A model-table row MUST store its provider in a field separate from its model.
  • A request MUST carry the model id stored in the selected model-table row.
  • sc-agent MUST be able to send requests through Together.
  • sc-agent MUST be able to send requests through OpenRouter.
  • When configuration names a provider for a model, sc-agent MUST send that model's requests to that provider.
  • When no provider is configured for a model, sc-agent MUST prefer a provider that needs no key over one that needs a key.
  • When no provider is configured for a model and every provider serving it needs a key, sc-agent MUST use the first of them whose key is found.
  • The provider that sends requests to the OpenAI API MUST have the name `openai`.
  • A short name MUST NOT encode its provider.
  • A request MUST NOT require the caller to name a provider.

Requirement

Definitions: sc-agent is this project's client library and command-line tool that sends model requests. A provider is the service a request is sent to, such as OpenRouter, Nous, Together, OpenAI or Anthropic. A model is what that provider runs. A model id is the name a provider uses for a model, such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` at OpenRouter. A short name is the name a caller uses for a model, such as `haiku`. The model table is the list of models sc-agent can send to, one row per model and provider (REQ-SAG-0102). A key is the secret credential a provider requires before it accepts a request; a keyless provider requires none. The OpenAI API is the request service run by OpenAI.

Rationale

The owner uses OpenRouter, Nous, Together, OpenAI and Anthropic today, and one model can be served by more than one provider. Making the caller pick a provider per call is poor UX and unreliable over time. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • Unit test: every model-table row stores its provider in a field separate from its model.
  • Unit test: a short name served by two providers is the same string for both rows.
  • Unit test: the short name `haiku` selects the same model through two different providers, and each sends its own id: `claude-haiku-5-5` through `anthropic` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` through `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: with `openrouter` configured for `haiku` and the `anthropic` key also found, a `haiku` request goes to `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: with no provider configured, a model served by a keyless provider and a keyed provider goes to the keyless one.
  • Unit test: with no provider configured and only the `openrouter` key found, a `haiku` request goes to `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: requests can be sent through `together` and through `openrouter`.
  • Unit test: a request that names only a model, with no provider, is sent.
  • Unit test: the provider that sends to the OpenAI API is named `openai`.

REQ-SAG-0901 LLM decision backends return the Jev schema

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.0

Statements

  • In decider mode, the covered model answering the request MUST itself generate the `probabilities` value when the required schema includes that field.
  • In decider mode, the covered model answering the request MUST itself generate the `confidence` value when the required schema includes that field.
  • In decider mode, answers from each covered model MUST conform to the required schema.
  • Each decision request MUST specify the required schema through the provider's structured-output feature.
  • If a provider response fails to match the required schema, the decision backend MUST return `decision.schema_mismatch`.
  • The covered model handling the decision request MUST pass the request's inputs to the provider.
  • If the provider rejects a request input, the decision backend MUST return the provider's error.

Requirement

Definitions: Decider mode uses a large language model, such as Haiku or Luna, to answer a decision request in place of a decision model. The covered models are Haiku and Luna. The provider is the service to which the decision request is sent. The required schema is the Jev decision API's answer schema for the requested question type, including `probabilities` and `confidence` where Jev returns them. The provider's structured-output feature lets a request specify the schema the provider's answer must follow. A `decision.schema_mismatch` error identifies what in the provider response failed to match the required schema.

Rationale

Callers compare Jev and LLM answers directly, so every backend must return the same answer shape. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A Haiku or Luna answer to a choice, score, noul and box question parses as the Jev answer type for that question.
  • A test provider that returns a response missing `probabilities` yields `decision.schema_mismatch`.

REQ-SAG-0801 Local decision runners come from configuration

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.7.0

Statements

  • Each local decision runner's network address MUST come from configuration.
  • Each local decision runner's model MUST have a fixed model id in the model table.
  • A selection of `decider` MUST resolve to the 4b decider model.
  • Each local decision runner MUST be selectable by its name wherever a decision model is selected.
  • Configuration MUST be able to add a local model that runs on another computer.
  • `sc-agent` MUST NOT hard-code the network address of any local decision runner.

Requirement

Definitions: The Jev API is the request and reply format of TypeSafe's Jev decision service (ADR-SAG-0001). A local decision runner is a daemon on the user's machine or network that serves a decision model through the Jev API. sc-agent has two, `laya` and `decider`. A runner's network address is its host and port. A decision model is a model that `sc-agent` can send a decision request to. The 4b decider model is the `decider-4b-v2.1` row. A local model is a model-table row whose model is served by a local decision runner. A paid API is a provider that needs an API key; its key is sent only to the provider's built-in endpoint.

Rationale

People are building local runners that duplicate the Jev API, and they differ only in where they run and how they report their loaded models. decider is an alternative local model to laya with a different connection string. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A unit test sets `laya.host` and `laya.port` in configuration and checks the request goes to them with no rebuild.
  • A unit test finds a fixed model id in the model-table row of every local decision runner model.
  • A unit test resolves `decider` to the 4b decider row.
  • A CLI run of each command that selects a decision model accepts `--model laya` and `--model decider`.
  • A unit test with a stub local runner checks that the request it receives is in the Jev API format.
  • A unit test sends to a local model row added in configuration with another computer's host and checks the request reaches that host.
  • A search of the whole workspace, outside tests, finds no host or port literal for a local runner.
  • A unit test with configuration naming another endpoint for a paid provider checks that the provider's key is still sent only to its built-in endpoint.

REQ-SAG-0701 Batches of decision requests run in parallel

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Statements

  • `sc-agent`'s `send_batch` MUST run the requests of one batch in parallel across workers.
  • The number of workers MUST be the `workers` setting.
  • When `workers` is not set, the number of workers MUST be 8.
  • Each result MUST carry the session ULID of the request it answers.
  • Each result MUST carry the input position of the request it answers.
  • A failed request MUST be returned as that request's error result.
  • When one request fails, the other requests of the batch MUST still run.
  • Cancelling the batch MUST stop every request that has not finished.

Requirement

Definitions: A batch is the decision requests a caller passes in one call: one JSONL file, one stdin stream or one Python call. A worker sends one request at a time. A session ULID (Universally Unique Lexicographically Sortable Identifier) is the `session_id` of the session row that records a request's result. Results may be returned in any order. `send_batch` is the sc-agent function that takes a batch and returns one result per request. A session row is the record sc-agent stores for each answered request. A request's input position is its zero-based index in the batch. An error result is a result that carries the request's error in place of an answer. A cache hit is a request whose successful result is served from an existing session row (REQ-SAG-0703).

Rationale

Tasks send tens of thousands of decisions, and one slow or failed request must not hold up or stop the others. Owner ruling (2026-11-20), Rand Lee: "I do not require results in request order." Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • With the default of 8 workers, a batch of 40 requests sent to a test server that holds every reply until 8 requests are in flight completes, and the server never sees more than 8 requests in flight.
  • Unit test: with the number of workers set to 1 in configuration, the test server never sees more than one request in flight from the same batch.
  • In a batch of 3 requests, each result carries the input position (0, 1 or 2) of the request it answers.
  • A batch in which one request fails returns that error tagged with its session ULID and returns every other result.
  • Cancelling a running batch returns cancelled results for every unfinished request.
  • A batch request that is a cache hit returns the `session_id` of the row that already holds its result.

REQ-SAG-0303 PyO3 and CLI query surfaces

REQ · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.2.1
