Requirement

Definitions: CLI means command-line interface. A loaded grammar is a tree-sitter grammar loaded by `sc-treesitter`. The PyO3 bindings expose the Python query interface to `sc-treesitter`. The `sitr` CLI can expose a subset of the PyO3 query surface.

Rationale

Python callers need full query access; the CLI runs specific predefined queries that simplify common use. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: every CLI has `--version`. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Acceptance criteria

  • A query written by the caller runs through the PyO3 bindings and returns its matches.
  • `languages` lists the loaded grammars and `queries` lists the predefined queries.
  • `sitr --version` prints the version.

ADR-SAG-0001 Every decision provider receives one request form

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Context

sc-agent sends decisions to Jev, to local runners that serve the Jev API, and to LLM backends such as Haiku and Luna.

Problem

Jev, local Jev-compatible runners, Haiku and Luna must answer the same decision so their answers can be compared, without shared crates knowing how any one backend adapts it.

Decision

For decision requests, every decision provider receives the same Jev API request body. `sc-agent` holds one provider table and one model table; the model table is its built-in rows plus the rows configuration adds (REQ-SAG-0102), so a new model works without a release. Decision providers implement one decision trait, and LLM providers one LLM trait (JSON in, JSON out). Jev implements the decision trait over SystemOne. One type per wire format, OpenAI-compatible chat/completions and Anthropic-compatible Messages, implements both traits and is shared by every provider of that format. Before a send, the decision implementation adapts the request to its wire format; the reply is decoded back into a Jev API response. Callers open one `Run` per command (created, used for its calls, then disposed) and use its two methods, `send` for one request and `send_batch` for many; the worker threads, holdoff, cancellation and session logging live behind them.

Key principles

  • There is one decision request form: the Jev API request body.
  • `send_batch` returns each result as it is ready, tagged with its session ULID and input position; a failed request is returned in its result and the batch continues.

Rationale

When every backend receives the same data, their answers are comparable by construction, and shared code stays free of provider-specific types. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md. Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "I do not require results in request order."

Positive consequences

A new provider is added as a table row, with no change to shared types.

ADR-SAG-0002 Session logs are JSONL first, then SQLite with server sync

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.3.0

Context

The owner builds tools that read session logs to tune consumer code, analysing 10,000 to 20,000 or more decisions at a time. One task produced 40,000 sessions, each a single Jev query with its own ULID and question digest.

Problem

Session logs must be separable by repository, type of work and project, kept indefinitely, and storable long term on a server.

Decision

For the MVP, session logs are JSONL under `<log_root>/sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/` (ADR-SAG-0021). Later they load into a local SQLite database that syncs to a server for long-term storage. Every row carries its own `session_id`, `repo`, `project` and `agent_role`. All sessions of one repo, agent role and project are appended to one file in that directory; a project lasts under a day to several days.

Key principles

  • Every row describes itself, so it stays meaningful when moved or loaded.
  • Session logs are never rotated or deleted.

Rationale

JSONL is simple to write and to read with the owner's tools now. Self-describing rows load into SQLite without parsing paths, and SQLite gives indexed retrieval of a response by its question digest.

Positive consequences

Path globs select a repository, role or project without opening files.

Negative consequences

Until the SQLite stage, retrieving a response by digest needs a load of the JSONL rows.

ADR-SAG-0003 Requirements and decisions are Raptor records

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Context

Requirements, non-functional requirements and architecture decisions are read by agents and by Raptor. The problem is that free-form records cannot be reliably imported into Raptor for tools to query and judge.

Decision

Every REQ, NFR and ADR is one Markdown file written from the Raptor authoring templates (`req-new.md.j2`, `nfr-new.md.j2`, `adr-new.md.j2` in randlee/raptor). Repository-wide records are under `docs/requirements/`, `docs/nfr/` and `docs/adr/`; crate-specific records are under the same folders inside `docs/<crate>/`. Changes to any record are made only in plan review and approved by the owner.

Rationale

Records that import into Raptor with no diagnostics can be queried and judged by tools, and owner approval in plan review keeps every change deliberate.

Positive consequences

Every record imports into Raptor and can be queried.

Negative consequences

Records are edited through templates, not by hand.

ADR-SAG-0004 Crate layering and error values

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.5.0

Context

sc-agent will launch decision models, LLMs, CLI agents and SDK agents. Each needs shared types, configuration, secrets, HTTP and logging, but not each other's code.

Problem

Crates must be layered so each launcher depends only on what it uses, and errors must keep every lower-layer id and message.

Decision

Crates are in four layers, and a crate depends only on crates in lower layers. Layer 1, core types and traits: `sc-agent-schema`, `sc-agent-sqlite`, `sc-agent-types`, `sc-agent-config`, `sc-agent-log`. Layer 2, one crate per API shape: `sc-decision-systemone`, `sc-anthropic`, `sc-openai`. Layer 3, shared behaviour and the API: `sc-decision-runner`, `sc-llm`. Layer 4, thin public surface: the `decidr` CLI and the Python wheel. `sitr` on `sc-treesitter` is a separate stack. Behaviour shared by crates in one layer is placed in a lower layer. A difference between them stays in the higher layer. A provider, a model and a URL are data: adding one changes configuration and no Rust code. CLI agents and SDK agents get their own crates later. Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message. A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002). An error may carry more fields. Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.

Key principles

  • A crate depends only on lower layers.
  • Shared behaviour moves down; differences move up.
  • A provider is a configuration row, not code.

Rationale

Layers let behaviour that several crates share be written once in a lower layer, and let a new provider or model be added without a code change. Owner ruling (2026-11-27), Rand Lee: "You need to be able to push shared methods down and move differences up" Owner ruling (2026-11-27), Rand Lee: "How do you extent to an 'unknown provider' or model' if you need to change rust when a model/provider is added, the architecture = fail. provider/model/url is just a string-tuple." Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "Errors are discriminated unions Result<t,e> I don't care about per crate"; "Extra fields are fine, make sure adr doesn't limit too much. I don't want findings for returning more." Owner ruling (2026-11-21), Rand Lee: "always return descriminated unions w/ error info"

Positive consequences

A new provider or model is a configuration row. A new API shape is one new layer 2 crate.

Negative consequences

More crates to version and publish than one core crate.

ADR-SAG-0005 sitr's Python API is built into the sc-decidr wheel; sitr is its own crate

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Context

sc-treesitter is the tree-sitter library with two query surfaces: the Python API and the `sitr` CLI.

Problem

The Python bindings and the CLI need PyO3 and clap, but a Rust caller of the library needs neither.

Decision

`sc-agent-py`, the crate that builds the sc-decidr wheel, depends on `sc-treesitter` and exposes the sitr Python API as `sc_agent.sitr`; there is no `sc-treesitter-py` crate (ADR-SAG-0021). There is no separate sitr wheel in phase h; a standalone sitr wheel may return after the MVP, and a process uses either it or the sc-decidr wheel, never both. The `sitr` binary is its own crate, `sitr`, over `sc-treesitter`. `sc-treesitter` has no PyO3 and no clap.

Key principles

  • `sc-treesitter` pulls in no PyO3 or clap.
  • The one Python extension module is built from `sc-agent-py`, not from `sc-treesitter`.

Rationale

Keeping PyO3 in `sc-agent-py` and clap in `sitr` keeps the library's dependency set small; building the sitr API into the sc-decidr wheel gives a Python process one copy of sc-observability and one Logger for decidr and sitr calls (ADR-SAG-0021). Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Positive consequences

A Rust caller of `sc-treesitter` compiles no Python or CLI dependencies.

Negative consequences

Installing the wheel always installs both the decidr and sitr APIs.

ADR-SAG-0017 First release surfaces

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.4.0

Context

Phase A ships libraries, the **decidr** decision CLI, the **sitr** tree-sitter CLI, and one Python wheel. Release must use one manifest-driven kit across five consumer channels. The problem is that every channel must release from the same tag, and per-channel workflow literals for crate lists or binary names would let the channels list different crates or binaries.

Decision

Phase A first release surfaces are **crates.io** (the crates listed in `release/publish-artifacts.toml`), **PyPI** (the `sc-decidr` wheel, holding the decidr and sitr APIs), **Homebrew**, **Scoop**, and **WinGet** (archives containing **decidr** and **sitr**), plus GitHub Release assets from the same tag. Sprints **a-11** (kit install) and **a-12** (dry-run) close the publish requirements; production uploads wait for owner dispatch.

Key principles

  • Customer-facing CLI names on channels are **decidr** and **sitr**.
  • The PyPI distribution name is **sc-decidr**.
  • No ad-hoc per-channel workflow literals for crate lists or binary names.

Rationale

- One manifest-driven kit drives all five consumer channels from the same tag. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Positive consequences

One tag drives every channel from `release/publish-artifacts.toml`.

Negative consequences

Workspace `Cargo.toml` must list members literally for kit validation.

ADR-SAG-0018 sc-publish kit owns release surface

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.1.1

Context

Release workflows, channel contracts, and `publish-artifacts.toml` are rendered from consumer input by [sc-publish](https://github.com/randlee/sc-publish). The problem is keeping the rendered release files consistent with that input and the pinned kit.

Decision

Edit `release/sc-publish-consumer-input.json` and re-run `install.py` from the pinned kit; do not hand-edit rendered files under `release/` or kit-owned `.github/workflows` publish YAML except through the installer.

Key principles

  • Pin a single qualified 40-character kit SHA in `release/sc-publish-pin.toml`.
  • Consumer input is the sole source of crate order, binaries, channels, and optional **docli** preflight checks.

Rationale

- The pinned kit renders release workflows and channel contracts from consumer input.

Positive consequences

Kit upgrades flow through pin bump + dry-run.

Negative consequences

Drift between JSON and rendered TOML is a hard fail until re-install.

ADR-SAG-0019 sc-decidr is the one Python decision harness

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 2.0.0

Context

sc-decidr is the harness through which sc-agent's Python consumers reach decision models (Jev, decider, Laya, Haiku, Luna). The owner requires judge-jev, plan-anchor and every later consumer to integrate identically for errors, API keys, model selection, the injectable general logger and session logging, differing only in prompt authoring and result handling. The two existing consumers each rebuilt the wheel boundary, and the copies diverged: judge-jev pins an id list with a `JEV.UNMAPPED` fallback while plan-anchor matches message text (`"http 401"`); plan-anchor pins `provider="typesafe"`, disabling Haiku and Luna; both re-sort `send_batch` results; judge-jev refuses `--timeout` while plan-anchor calls the unreleased `timeout_secs`. Consumers had no category to branch on and no per-call worker count or timeout.

Decision

The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3. 1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path. **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged. - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping. - model selectors are Run arguments. - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path. - Python results are typed values, not dicts. - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced. **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library. 2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.

Rationale

Two consumers rebuilt the boundary and diverged, so the boundary moves into the wheel and integration code is generated from one template. A stored category and the send count replace message parsing and pinned id lists, and per-run limits and position-tagged results remove consumer workarounds.

Positive consequences

  • Every Python consumer renders the same integration module and holds only its prompts and result handling.
  • No consumer parses error text or pins id lists, and all Jev data takes one session-log path.

Negative consequences

The wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout.

ADR-SAG-0020 Configuration has a shared scope and one scope per CLI, each global and per worktree

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.6.0

Context

sc-agent ships two CLIs today, `decidr` and `sitr`. CLI launchers for other agent harnesses, such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Hermes and pi-agent, will be added as their peers. Apps such as plan-anchor and judge-jev wrap a CLI the way a named agent (`.claude/agents/<agent>.md`) wraps a harness. Agent-level settings, for agents such as `lai`, `sai`, `sanity`, `plan-anchor` and `judge-jev`, will later be provided by the CLI launchers. Before this decision, every CLI read one shared file pair, `~/.sc-agent/default.json` and `~/.sc-agent/local.json`, with `SC_AGENT__<KEY>` environment overrides. That layout has no per-CLI settings and no per-repository layer: two worktrees of one repository cannot hold different settings, and a setting meant for one CLI applies to all of them.

Problem

Each CLI needs its own settings, shared defaults may be overridden by a CLI file, and a repository or worktree must be able to override both.

Decision

Configuration has two kinds of scope and two locations. - The shared scope is the file `sc-agent.json`. It holds shared defaults for configuration-reading CLIs: the project/phase (ADR-SAG-0021), worker count, and optional local-runner settings. A CLI file may override those defaults. - Each CLI that reads configuration has its own scope, the file `<cli>.json` named after the CLI: `decidr.json`, and the same pattern for every CLI added later. `sitr` reads no configuration. - The global location is `~/.sc-agent/`, the user's home directory joined with `.sc-agent` on every platform, or the folder named by nonempty `SC_AGENT_HOME`. An explicit configuration directory takes precedence. - The local location is `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/`, where `<worktree>` is the root of the git work tree the CLI runs in. It holds the same file names with the same keys. The CLIs and the files each one reads are these: | CLI | Global files | Local files | Environment prefix | |---|---|---|---| | `decidr` | `~/.sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `~/.sc-agent/decidr.json`, `~/.sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `DECIDR_`, plus `SC_PROJECT` | | `sitr` | none | none | none | Every CLI has a row, and every cell is filled; a CLI that reads no file of a kind says `none`. The table is updated when a CLI is added. A setting is looked up in nine layers, and the first layer that sets it wins: 1. the CLI flag; 2. the environment variable; 3. the local `<cli>.local.json`; 4. the local `<cli>.json`; 5. the local `sc-agent.json`; 6. the global `<cli>.local.json`; 7. the global `<cli>.json`; 8. the global `sc-agent.json`; 9. the built-in default. Model entries, `models.<alias>`, are set only in configuration files, layers 3 to 8: each is a structured row (`provider` and `id` strings, `released` a `YYYY-MM-DD` date) that a flag or flat environment variable cannot express. `<alias>` becomes the row's short name. A row's provider is one sc-agent already has. Environment variables are named after the CLI: `DECIDR_<SETTING>`, with the parts of a nested key joined by a double underscore (`DECIDR_LAYA__PORT`). A setting with a wider audience than sc-agent may have its own name; the project/phase is `SC_PROJECT` (ADR-SAG-0021). Configuration files are JSON. TOML will be added when sc-config supports it (randlee/sc-runtime#152).

Key principles

  • A narrower location beats a wider one: local beats global.
  • Within one location, a CLI's own file beats the shared file.
  • sc ecosystem files in a repository live under `.sc/`, so a repository needs one `.gitignore` entry rather than one per tool.

Rationale

One file per CLI keeps each CLI's settings separate and lets a new CLI be added without touching another CLI's file. The shared file gives one place for shared defaults that a CLI file may override. The local location under `.sc/` lets each worktree differ, which matters because worktrees of one repository often work on different phases at the same time. Env vars named after the CLI keep one CLI's override from reaching another. Owner ruling 2026-11-21: records follow docs/plans/reduction-plan.md.

Positive consequences

  • A CLI added later gets its own global and local file without a schema change to any other file.
  • A worktree can override any setting without editing the user's global files.

Negative consequences

A setting can now come from nine places; `decidr doctor` reports a `path | value | source` table.

ADR-SAG-0021 One sc-observability Logger per process, owned by the entry point; general logs and session logs in separate trees

ADR · sc-agent · Approved · version 0.9.0

Context

sc-agent logs through sc-observability. The `decidr` CLI, the `sitr` CLI and the sc-decidr wheel already link the sc-observability crate. Two kinds of log exist: the general log (diagnostics, searched for issues) and session logs (the long-term record of every successful model query and its response, analysed later and loaded into SQLite, ADR-SAG-0002).

Problem

Every general-log record of a process must reach one Logger that the process's entry point owns, and every log must land at a fixed, known path, with session logs never mixed with general logs.

Decision

**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client. The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed. The generated client has no close operation. Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`. **The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls; Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue. **Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product. | Product | Contains | |---|---| | `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability | | `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability | | sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability | There is one Python wheel. A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike. Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses. **Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below. Every decision and sitr call is logged. A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility. **Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink. **Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004). | Entry point | General log | Session logs | |---|---|---| | `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none | | `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added. **Session identity.** - `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting. - `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.

Key principles

  • One process, one general Logger, one queue, owned by the entry point; session rows and link records go through sc-agent's session sink, never the general Logger.
  • Session logs and general logs are never written to the same folder tree.
  • A session is never filed under a guessed project/phase.

Rationale

The entry point is the only code that knows the process's lifetime, so it is the only correct owner of the Logger: it obtains the Logger before the first general-log record and flushes after each call. Exposing the crate's own Logger from the wheel keeps one copy and one queue in the process and needs no Python package. Fixed paths keep every log in one known place for audit, and a separate `sessions/` tree lets tools and the later SQLite load read every session with a path glob. The session log is the record of every successful Jev query from every tool, so it cannot be turned off and is never rotated; it stays small enough because `project` changes over time.

Positive consequences

  • Libraries hold no logging policy: they take a Logger or use the default.
  • `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/` selects one agent's work in one phase with a path glob.

Negative consequences

Every caller must supply a project/phase before its first request.

ANC-001

Statement

The decidr model name `jev` must select the newest Jev model in sc-agent's model table unless a config file sets another default, so callers get the latest Jev without a code change.

Owner said

I want 'jev' to select latest, config can override default.

Scope

adds or changes model resolution, the model table or the jev alias in sc-agent or decidr

Deterministic check

unit test: resolve("jev") == first Jev row of the date-sorted table; with config default set, == configured id

Kind

directive

Stated by

Rand Lee

Stated on

2026-11-26

ANC-002

Statement

Until SQLite schema 1.0, sc-agent, judge-jev and plan-anchor must read only the record schema version they write and contain no reader for an older version, so read and write stay in step.

Owner said

ADR-SAG-0021 × ANC-023 — conflicts

sc-agent

What conflicts

  • “**Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink.”

This ADR specifies a JSONL session and run log layout, which conflicts with the owner's SQLite ruling. The complete ADR decision is multi-topic, so this trace item does not isolate a safe edit that preserves its other decisions.

No owner-ready change proposed; review a focused rewrite of the session-log section.

Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink.”: Its JSONL session-store details predate the 2026-11-27 SQLite directions, but the cell does not isolate which detailed clauses should change.

REQ-SAG-0002 × ANC-021 — related

sc-agent

Anchor

Every phase-m sprint bead names the crate and layer each change lands in, and that layer is the lowest layer whose crates all use the change.

Owner said: “You need to be able to push shared methods down and move differences up”

Scope: adds or changes code in any crate under crates/

Record statements

  • Every public API MUST return a discriminated union of success and error.
  • Rust APIs MUST return `Result<T, E>` from the lowest layer to the top-level CLI and PyO3 entry points.
  • An error MUST carry the error id and message of every lower-layer error that caused it.
  • A layer that changes an error MUST change it only by adding detail.
  • Error text received from a provider MUST be kept whole.
  • Exception (owner-approved): the API key MUST never appear in an error or log.
  • Every error MUST have a stable id.
  • Rust code MUST NOT panic on any input or runtime failure.
  • A layer MUST NOT drop or replace a lower-layer error id or message.

  • A CLI MUST NOT read another CLI's `<cli>.json`.

written by the anchor-cleanup-proposer agent, not Jev

Anchor

The sc-agent model table must accept extra model rows from config in addition to its hard-coded rows, so a new model works without waiting for a release.

Record statements

  • A model-table row MUST store its provider in a field separate from its model.

  • A short name MUST NOT encode its provider.
  • A request MUST NOT require the caller to name a provider.

REQ-SAG-0601 × ANC-030 — exceeds

sc-agent

Proposals: 10

What exceeds

  • “When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.”
  • “Every later send to the provider endpoint MUST wait until the endpoint's not-before time.”

These clauses place shared host holdoff state and send waiting inside `HttpClient`; the later owner ruling calls for retry and holdoff inputs to be parameterized by the calling layer.

Proposed remedy

written by the anchor-cleanup-proposer agent, not Jev

Delete the two client-specific holdoff mechanics.

Stale

written by the anchor-cleanup-proposer agent, not Jev

REQ-SAG-0601 “When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.”: The clauses were added 2026-11-24, before the owner's 2026-11-27 parameterization ruling.

Anchor

Retry and holdoff code takes its waits, limits and busy and quota rules as parameters from the calling layer, and contains no provider name, host or status-code table.

Owner said: “retry and holdoff are pushed down as far as possible w/ info/data patameterized coming from implementation.”

Scope: adds or changes retry, resend, backoff or holdoff code

Record statements

  • A request that receives a busy response MUST be resent unchanged.
  • A request whose send has a network failure MUST be resent unchanged, counting toward the same maximum number of sends.
  • The maximum number of sends per request MUST be a configurable maximum, 5 by default.
  • When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.
  • Every later send to the provider endpoint MUST wait until the endpoint's not-before time.
  • When the provider gives a `Retry-After`, it MUST set the holdoff.
  • When the provider gives no `Retry-After`, the holdoffs MUST back off exponentially; this requirement does not fix their values.
  • A held-off request MUST wait in the queue until its holdoff ends, and the wait MUST end at once when the request is cancelled.
  • When sends run out on busy replies, the error MUST say busy, with the send count.
  • Authentication (401) and quota MUST NOT be resent; they MUST be returned with the remote error id and message.

ADR-SAG-0001 Every decision provider receives one request form

Decision

For decision requests, every decision provider receives the same Jev API request body. `sc-agent` holds one provider table and one model table; the model table is its built-in rows plus the rows configuration adds (REQ-SAG-0102), so a new model works without a release. Decision providers implement one decision trait, and LLM providers one LLM trait (JSON in, JSON out). Jev implements the decision trait over SystemOne. One type per wire format, OpenAI-compatible chat/completions and Anthropic-compatible Messages, implements both traits and is shared by every provider of that format. Before a send, the decision implementation adapts the request to its wire format; the reply is decoded back into a Jev API response. Callers open one `Run` per command (created, used for its calls, then disposed) and use its two methods, `send` for one request and `send_batch` for many; the worker threads, holdoff, cancellation and session logging live behind them.

REQ-SAG-0901 LLM decision backends return the Jev schema

Statements

  • In decider mode, the covered model answering the request MUST itself generate the `probabilities` value when the required schema includes that field.
  • In decider mode, the covered model answering the request MUST itself generate the `confidence` value when the required schema includes that field.
  • In decider mode, answers from each covered model MUST conform to the required schema.
  • Each decision request MUST specify the required schema through the provider's structured-output feature.
  • If a provider response fails to match the required schema, the decision backend MUST return `decision.schema_mismatch`.
  • The covered model handling the decision request MUST pass the request's inputs to the provider.
  • If the provider rejects a request input, the decision backend MUST return the provider's error.

REQ-SAG-0004 Session log identity: repo, agent role, project and tool

Statements

  • Every session row MUST carry its identity.
  • sc-agent MUST refuse every query whose identity is not valid.
  • In a git repository, a query's repository MUST be that repository's origin name.

  • The `decidr` CLI MUST accept an agent role from its user.
  • The Python bindings of sc-agent MUST accept an agent role from their caller.
  • A generated consumer client MUST set the agent role to the client's product name.
  • A generated consumer client MUST NOT let its user set the agent role.

ADR-SAG-0004 Crate layering and error values

Decision

Crates are in four layers, and a crate depends only on crates in lower layers. Layer 1, core types and traits: `sc-agent-schema`, `sc-agent-sqlite`, `sc-agent-types`, `sc-agent-config`, `sc-agent-log`. Layer 2, one crate per API shape: `sc-decision-systemone`, `sc-anthropic`, `sc-openai`. Layer 3, shared behaviour and the API: `sc-decision-runner`, `sc-llm`. Layer 4, thin public surface: the `decidr` CLI and the Python wheel. `sitr` on `sc-treesitter` is a separate stack. Behaviour shared by crates in one layer is placed in a lower layer. A difference between them stays in the higher layer. A provider, a model and a URL are data: adding one changes configuration and no Rust code. CLI agents and SDK agents get their own crates later. Errors are discriminated unions: every call returns `Result<T, E>`, and `E` carries the error info: at least an id and a message. A layer that changes an error keeps the lower error's id and message (REQ-SAG-0002). An error may carry more fields. Whether a crate has its own error type or shares one is not specified.

REQ-SAG-0002 Errors are a discriminated union carried from bottom to top

Statements

  • Every public API MUST return a discriminated union of success and error.
  • Rust APIs MUST return `Result<T, E>` from the lowest layer to the top-level CLI and PyO3 entry points.
  • An error MUST carry the error id and message of every lower-layer error that caused it.
  • A layer that changes an error MUST change it only by adding detail.
  • Error text received from a provider MUST be kept whole.
  • Exception (owner-approved): the API key MUST never appear in an error or log.
  • Every error MUST have a stable id.
  • Rust code MUST NOT panic on any input or runtime failure.
  • A layer MUST NOT drop or replace a lower-layer error id or message.

ADR-SAG-0019 sc-decidr is the one Python decision harness

Decision

The wheel is the one consumer boundary. Decision numbers are stable; there is no decision 3. 1. **The wheel is the consumer boundary.** Every consumer concern except prompt authoring and result interpretation belongs in sc-decidr: model selection, API keys (environment, repo-root `.env`, OS keyring), session logging, the general Logger, errors with a stored category (decisions 2, 5 and 6), limits and cancellation (decisions 7 and 14) and position-tagged batch results (decision 8). Session logging is always on: one row per query whose model call succeeded (a failed call writes no row; its error goes to the general log), at the wheel's default location, tagged with `project` and `agent_role`, written by sc-agent's session sink (ADR-SAG-0021); a cache hit writes no row and one link record (REQ-SAG-0005, REQ-SAG-0703). All Jev queries and responses therefore take one path. **The integration artifact is a generated module** (REQ-SAG-0018), rendered by each consumer from the sc-compose template `sc_agent/templates/consumer.py.j2`; the wheel moves to maturin's mixed layout and `import sc_agent` is unchanged. - The template covers the decision call, model pass-through, logging wiring, cancellation and the error-to-category-to-code mapping. - model selectors are Run arguments. - A result line holds only the generic result fields; session data stays in the session row. The module reads session rows only through `sc_agent.session_rows`, finding a run's queries through its link records or the session_ids in its result lines, and never computes a session-log path. - Python results are typed values, not dicts. - sc-compose is an external render tool, not a wheel dependency; the template's front matter declares its sc-compose minimum (`requires.cli`), declared, not enforced. **The lower-level API stays the contract.** `Run` (with `send` and `send_batch`), `session_rows`, `provider_keys`, `TYPESAFE`, `digest`, `logger`, `log`, `flush` and `sc_agent.sitr` are public, and the generated code uses only them and the standard library. 2. **Typed fields: `attempts` and `category`.** An error value carries at least `id`, `message` and `action`, plus `attempts` (sends made, the first included) and `category` (decision 6) when they apply; unset fields are not written (REQ-SAG-0016). Retry-After is read as a Duration and used for the wait before a resend (REQ-SAG-0601). 5. **Python errors.** Every wheel call returns ok with a value or an error with its id and message; nothing raises (REQ-SAG-0016). 6. **The category is stored when the error is built.** The categories are `busy`, `quota`, `auth`, `network`, `response_invalid`, `validation`, `cancelled`, `config`, `log` and `other`. Every error has a stable id and stores its category, which Python reads from the `category` field (REQ-SAG-0017). Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.

REQ-SAG-0002 Errors are a discriminated union carried from bottom to top

Statements

  • Every public API MUST return a discriminated union of success and error.
  • Rust APIs MUST return `Result<T, E>` from the lowest layer to the top-level CLI and PyO3 entry points.
  • An error MUST carry the error id and message of every lower-layer error that caused it.
  • A layer that changes an error MUST change it only by adding detail.
  • Error text received from a provider MUST be kept whole.
  • Exception (owner-approved): the API key MUST never appear in an error or log.
  • Every error MUST have a stable id.
  • Rust code MUST NOT panic on any input or runtime failure.
  • A layer MUST NOT drop or replace a lower-layer error id or message.

Retryable means worth resubmitting as a new call later, after the wheel's own resends have run out; it is true for `busy` and `network` only, and a consumer that resubmits waits first rather than wrapping the wheel in an immediate retry loop. 7. **Per-run limits: `timeout_secs` and `workers`.** A Run takes an optional timeout (a Duration) and worker count, for that Run's calls only (`--timeout-secs` and `--workers` on the CLI); `None` means the configured value, and every send, resends included, gets the full timeout. The timeout defaults to 120 s; REQ-SAG-0702 holds the rules. 8. **`send_batch` returns one result per request, each with its input position**, while `on_result` still receives each line as it finishes (REQ-SAG-0702). 11. **sitr is an optional, separate section of the consumer template.** It uses `sc_agent.sitr` only (ADR-SAG-0005, ADR-SAG-0021) and is kept separate from the decision call: extraction runs outside the decision path, and its output feeds the consumer's prompt authoring. In this phase one offline test shows extraction output reaching a dry-run request. 14. **A run is a context object.** `sc_agent.Run(tool=, tool_version=, cache=, ...)` is created once per tool command and closed when its calls are done (`with sc_agent.Run(...) as run:`); creating it mints the run's ULID `run_id` in Rust (as are `session_id` ULIDs), readable as `run.run_id`.

REQ-SAG-0005 Session log rows and run links

Statements

  • Session logs MUST be written as JSONL.
  • For every query whose model call succeeded, sc-agent MUST append a session row to the query's session log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT append more than one session row for one query.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT append a session row for a failed call; the error goes to the general log.

REQ-SAG-0601 Busy resend and holdoff

Statements

  • A request that receives a busy response MUST be resent unchanged.
  • A request whose send has a network failure MUST be resent unchanged, counting toward the same maximum number of sends.
  • The maximum number of sends per request MUST be a configurable maximum, 5 by default.
  • When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.
  • Every later send to the provider endpoint MUST wait until the endpoint's not-before time.
  • When the provider gives a `Retry-After`, it MUST set the holdoff.
  • When the provider gives no `Retry-After`, the holdoffs MUST back off exponentially; this requirement does not fix their values.
  • A held-off request MUST wait in the queue until its holdoff ends, and the wait MUST end at once when the request is cancelled.
  • When sends run out on busy replies, the error MUST say busy, with the send count.
  • Authentication (401) and quota MUST NOT be resent; they MUST be returned with the remote error id and message.

ADR-SAG-0020 Configuration has a shared scope and one scope per CLI, each global and per worktree

Decision

Configuration has two kinds of scope and two locations. - The shared scope is the file `sc-agent.json`. It holds shared defaults for configuration-reading CLIs: the project/phase (ADR-SAG-0021), worker count, and optional local-runner settings. A CLI file may override those defaults. - Each CLI that reads configuration has its own scope, the file `<cli>.json` named after the CLI: `decidr.json`, and the same pattern for every CLI added later. `sitr` reads no configuration. - The global location is `~/.sc-agent/`, the user's home directory joined with `.sc-agent` on every platform, or the folder named by nonempty `SC_AGENT_HOME`. An explicit configuration directory takes precedence. - The local location is `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/`, where `<worktree>` is the root of the git work tree the CLI runs in. It holds the same file names with the same keys. The CLIs and the files each one reads are these: | CLI | Global files | Local files | Environment prefix | |---|---|---|---| | `decidr` | `~/.sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `~/.sc-agent/decidr.json`, `~/.sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `DECIDR_`, plus `SC_PROJECT` | | `sitr` | none | none | none | Every CLI has a row, and every cell is filled; a CLI that reads no file of a kind says `none`. The table is updated when a CLI is added. A setting is looked up in nine layers, and the first layer that sets it wins: 1. the CLI flag; 2. the environment variable; 3. the local `<cli>.local.json`; 4. the local `<cli>.json`; 5. the local `sc-agent.json`; 6. the global `<cli>.local.json`; 7. the global `<cli>.json`; 8. the global `sc-agent.json`; 9. the built-in default. Model entries, `models.<alias>`, are set only in configuration files, layers 3 to 8: each is a structured row (`provider` and `id` strings, `released` a `YYYY-MM-DD` date) that a flag or flat environment variable cannot express. `<alias>` becomes the row's short name. A row's provider is one sc-agent already has. Environment variables are named after the CLI: `DECIDR_<SETTING>`, with the parts of a nested key joined by a double underscore (`DECIDR_LAYA__PORT`). A setting with a wider audience than sc-agent may have its own name; the project/phase is `SC_PROJECT` (ADR-SAG-0021). Configuration files are JSON. TOML will be added when sc-config supports it (randlee/sc-runtime#152).

REQ-SAG-0019 Configuration file locations and lookup order

Statements

  • When a required setting has no built-in default and no layer sets it, the CLI MUST return a missing-setting error.
  • Each configuration file MUST accept the shared settings.
  • A CLI file MUST accept that CLI's settings.
  • An unknown key in a configuration file MUST cause a typed load error.
  • The `cache` setting MUST default to `true`.
  • A model entry MUST add one row to the model table.
  • A model entry MUST override the model its name selects.
  • A local endpoint's address MUST be settable in configuration.
  • When the CLI does not run inside a git work tree, it MUST skip the local-folder layers.
  • Each CLI's `<cli> doctor` command, such as `decidr doctor`, MUST report the settings table.
  • In each row of the settings table, the `source` cell MUST show the source of that row's value.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST report the path of every file in the nine layers.
  • For each file in the nine layers, `<cli> doctor` MUST report whether it exists.
  • When a CLI fails to load a configuration file, its error MUST name the failure location.

  • While it loads configuration, a CLI MUST NOT write to any configuration file.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST NOT send a model request.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST NOT write a file.
  • Configuration MUST NOT change a paid API's base address.

ADR-SAG-0020 Configuration has a shared scope and one scope per CLI, each global and per worktree

Decision

Configuration has two kinds of scope and two locations. - The shared scope is the file `sc-agent.json`. It holds shared defaults for configuration-reading CLIs: the project/phase (ADR-SAG-0021), worker count, and optional local-runner settings. A CLI file may override those defaults. - Each CLI that reads configuration has its own scope, the file `<cli>.json` named after the CLI: `decidr.json`, and the same pattern for every CLI added later. `sitr` reads no configuration. - The global location is `~/.sc-agent/`, the user's home directory joined with `.sc-agent` on every platform, or the folder named by nonempty `SC_AGENT_HOME`. An explicit configuration directory takes precedence. - The local location is `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/`, where `<worktree>` is the root of the git work tree the CLI runs in. It holds the same file names with the same keys. The CLIs and the files each one reads are these: | CLI | Global files | Local files | Environment prefix | |---|---|---|---| | `decidr` | `~/.sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `~/.sc-agent/decidr.json`, `~/.sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.local.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/decidr.json`, `<worktree>/.sc/sc-agent/sc-agent.json` | `DECIDR_`, plus `SC_PROJECT` | | `sitr` | none | none | none | Every CLI has a row, and every cell is filled; a CLI that reads no file of a kind says `none`. The table is updated when a CLI is added. A setting is looked up in nine layers, and the first layer that sets it wins: 1. the CLI flag; 2. the environment variable; 3. the local `<cli>.local.json`; 4. the local `<cli>.json`; 5. the local `sc-agent.json`; 6. the global `<cli>.local.json`; 7. the global `<cli>.json`; 8. the global `sc-agent.json`; 9. the built-in default. Model entries, `models.<alias>`, are set only in configuration files, layers 3 to 8: each is a structured row (`provider` and `id` strings, `released` a `YYYY-MM-DD` date) that a flag or flat environment variable cannot express. `<alias>` becomes the row's short name. A row's provider is one sc-agent already has. Environment variables are named after the CLI: `DECIDR_<SETTING>`, with the parts of a nested key joined by a double underscore (`DECIDR_LAYA__PORT`). A setting with a wider audience than sc-agent may have its own name; the project/phase is `SC_PROJECT` (ADR-SAG-0021). Configuration files are JSON. TOML will be added when sc-config supports it (randlee/sc-runtime#152).

REQ-SAG-0103 Provider and model are separate

Statements

  • A model-table row MUST store its provider in a field separate from its model.
  • A request MUST carry the model id stored in the selected model-table row.
  • sc-agent MUST be able to send requests through Together.
  • sc-agent MUST be able to send requests through OpenRouter.
  • When configuration names a provider for a model, sc-agent MUST send that model's requests to that provider.
  • When no provider is configured for a model, sc-agent MUST prefer a provider that needs no key over one that needs a key.
  • When no provider is configured for a model and every provider serving it needs a key, sc-agent MUST use the first of them whose key is found.
  • The provider that sends requests to the OpenAI API MUST have the name `openai`.
  • A short name MUST NOT encode its provider.
  • A request MUST NOT require the caller to name a provider.

ADR-SAG-0021 One sc-observability Logger per process, owned by the entry point; general logs and session logs in separate trees

Decision

**One Logger per process, owned by the entry point.** The entry point is the CLI's `main`, or, for a Python app, its sc-compose generated client. The entry point obtains one sc-observability `Logger`, keeps it for the life of the process and gives it to each Run it creates (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14); the Run passes it to every decision call, flushes it after each call and on exit, and never shuts down a Logger it borrowed. The generated client has no close operation. Library code never builds a Logger of its own while one is injected, and never forwards records to Python `logging`. **The wheel exposes the crate's Logger.** Python may write its own records to it and gives it to the Run of its sc-decidr calls; Rust receives its own Logger object back, so no record crosses a bridge and the process has one queue. **Products.** sc-agent ships three products. sc-observability is a crate linked into each, not a product. | Product | Contains | |---|---| | `decidr` CLI | decidr, sc-observability | | `sitr` CLI | sitr, sc-observability | | sc-decidr wheel | the decidr and sitr Python APIs, sc-observability | There is one Python wheel. A Python process that loads sc-agent has one copy of sc-observability and one Logger, which it injects into decidr and sitr calls alike. Installing the wheel always installs both APIs, whichever one the caller uses. **Defaults.** With no Logger injected, sc-agent uses the default sc-observability Logger, which writes the general log to disk at the paths below. Every decision and sitr call is logged. A caller that wants another general-log sink (a database, nothing) changes the sink of the Logger it injects; that is the caller's responsibility. **Session log.** The session log is always on and is not configurable. sc-agent writes every session row in Rust through its session sink. No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. The session row carries no `run_id`: runs and sessions are many-to-many, because a cache hit serves a later run from an older session. Each session row carries `provider` and `usage` (`null` when the reply reports none), `model_requested` (the resolved model id) and `model_answered` (the model id the response reported, `null` when no response arrived), and has no start or end time. Callers inject no session Logger and cannot replace the session sink. **Paths.** The log root is `~/.sc-agent`. One function returns a CLI's log root. The CLIs and the wheel call that function; nothing else computes a log path. The wheel's `sc_agent.session_rows(session_ids, *, agent_role, project=None)` is the one reader of the session-log layout: it finds the log root with the same function used to write session rows and returns, as an ok value, a map from each requested `session_id` to its row; a missing id returns `session.not_found` (category `validation`) naming the ids. A generated client reads session rows only through it and has no log-root argument (NFR-SAG-0004). | Entry point | General log | Session logs | |---|---|---| | `decidr` CLI | `logs/decidr.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/<agent_role>/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `sitr` CLI | `logs/sitr.log.jsonl` | none | | `plan-anchor` (generated client) | `logs/plan-anchor.log.jsonl` | `sessions/<repo>/plan-anchor/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | | `judge-jev` (generated client) | `logs/judge-jev.log.jsonl`, holding its decidr and sitr records | `sessions/<repo>/judge-jev/<project>/sessions.jsonl` | A wheel is not an entry point and has no row: it writes to the Logger its caller injects. Every entry point has a row and every cell is filled. The table is updated when an entry point is added. **Session identity.** - `agent_role` is the agent or app making the request. A generated client hardcodes it to its product name; it is not a user setting. - `tool` and `tool_version` name the program that sent the query and its version: the generated client's name, or `decidr` (REQ-SAG-0004). They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.

NFR-SAG-0001 Session logging at 40,000 sessions per task

Statements

  • All sessions of one repo, agent role and project MUST be written to one session log file.
  • Session logging MUST NOT create one log file per session.

REQ-SAG-0003 Log locations and retention

Statements

  • With no Logger injected, each CLI MUST write its general log to `~/.sc-agent/logs/<cli>.log.jsonl`.
  • When `<CLI>_LOG_ROOT` is set and non-empty, that CLI MUST use its value in place of `~/.sc-agent`.
  • When `<CLIENT>_LOG_ROOT` is set and not empty, the generated client MUST use that folder in place of `~/.sc-agent/` for its logs.
  • Session logs MUST be written under `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` (REQ-SAG-0005).
  • A session log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
  • A run log MUST remain in `~/.sc-agent/sessions/` whatever its age.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT contain code that removes a general log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT remove a session log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT remove a run log.

They are carried by the Run the query is sent through (ADR-SAG-0019 decision 14). - `project` is the project/phase, resolved by the configuration lookup of ADR-SAG-0020 (`--project`, `SC_PROJECT`, then the config files). It is required and has no default; a session without one is refused with a typed error naming every place it can be set. Usage, help and errors call it "project/phase". **Errors.** An error is logged once, in Rust, with the same id and fields whatever the harness, so the general logs can be searched with one set of terms. It is logged again only when an outer layer adds information that helps debugging. A failed `log.write` or `log.flush` returns the Logger's failure as an error value; nothing else handles it. A successful decision remains in its session row when general logging fails; the call returns the log error rather than that decision value.

REQ-SAG-0004 Session log identity: repo, agent role, project and tool

Statements

  • Every session row MUST carry its identity.
  • sc-agent MUST refuse every query whose identity is not valid.
  • In a git repository, a query's repository MUST be that repository's origin name.
  • Outside a git repository, a query's repository MUST be `local/<host>/<folder-name>`.
  • A query's project MUST be the project that REQ-SAG-0021 resolves for it.
  • The `decidr` CLI MUST accept an agent role from its user.
  • The Python bindings of sc-agent MUST accept an agent role from their caller.
  • A generated consumer client MUST set the agent role to the client's product name.
  • A generated consumer client MUST NOT let its user set the agent role.

No Logger sits between sc-agent and the session sink, and the session sink never receives a general-log record. A session sink of the same kind, opened on the run log, appends one link record `{run_id, session_id, cached}` to the run log, `runs.jsonl` beside `sessions.jsonl`, for every query that writes a session row (`cached: false`) and for every cache hit (`cached: true`); the run log is always on and never rotated or pruned either. REQ-SAG-0005 Session log rows and run links

Statements

  • Session logs MUST be written as JSONL.
  • For every query whose model call succeeded, sc-agent MUST append a session row to the query's session log.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT append more than one session row for one query.
  • sc-agent MUST NOT append a session row for a failed call; the error goes to the general log.

REQ-SAG-0021 The project/phase setting is required and shared

Statements

  • The `project` setting MUST be resolved through every project layer.
  • The PyO3 bindings MUST take `project` from the first project layer that sets it.
  • In the PyO3 bindings, a `project` argument MUST take the place of the `--project` flag layer.
  • A session with no project/phase MUST be refused with an error.
  • When no project layer sets `project`, a session write MUST NOT send a session.
  • When no project layer sets `project`, a session write MUST NOT write a session.
  • `project` MUST NOT have a built-in default.

REQ-SAG-0019 Configuration file locations and lookup order

Statements

  • When a required setting has no built-in default and no layer sets it, the CLI MUST return a missing-setting error.
  • Each configuration file MUST accept the shared settings.
  • A CLI file MUST accept that CLI's settings.
  • An unknown key in a configuration file MUST cause a typed load error.
  • The `cache` setting MUST default to `true`.
  • A model entry MUST add one row to the model table.
  • A model entry MUST override the model its name selects.
  • A local endpoint's address MUST be settable in configuration.
  • When the CLI does not run inside a git work tree, it MUST skip the local-folder layers.
  • Each CLI's `<cli> doctor` command, such as `decidr doctor`, MUST report the settings table.
  • In each row of the settings table, the `source` cell MUST show the source of that row's value.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST report the path of every file in the nine layers.
  • For each file in the nine layers, `<cli> doctor` MUST report whether it exists.
  • When a CLI fails to load a configuration file, its error MUST name the failure location.
  • A CLI MUST NOT read another CLI's `<cli>.json`.
  • While it loads configuration, a CLI MUST NOT write to any configuration file.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST NOT send a model request.
  • `<cli> doctor` MUST NOT write a file.
  • Configuration MUST NOT change a paid API's base address.

REQ-SAG-0801 Local decision runners come from configuration

Statements

  • Each local decision runner's network address MUST come from configuration.
  • Each local decision runner's model MUST have a fixed model id in the model table.
  • A selection of `decider` MUST resolve to the 4b decider model.
  • Each local decision runner MUST be selectable by its name wherever a decision model is selected.
  • Configuration MUST be able to add a local model that runs on another computer.
  • `sc-agent` MUST NOT hard-code the network address of any local decision runner.

REQ-SAG-0601 Busy resend and holdoff

Statements

  • A request that receives a busy response MUST be resent unchanged.
  • A request whose send has a network failure MUST be resent unchanged, counting toward the same maximum number of sends.
  • The maximum number of sends per request MUST be a configurable maximum, 5 by default.
  • When an `HttpClient` receives a busy reply from a host, the `HttpClient` MUST set a not-before time shared by every send through that client to that host.
  • Every later send to the provider endpoint MUST wait until the endpoint's not-before time.
  • When the provider gives a `Retry-After`, it MUST set the holdoff.
  • When the provider gives no `Retry-After`, the holdoffs MUST back off exponentially; this requirement does not fix their values.
  • A held-off request MUST wait in the queue until its holdoff ends, and the wait MUST end at once when the request is cancelled.
  • When sends run out on busy replies, the error MUST say busy, with the send count.
  • Authentication (401) and quota MUST NOT be resent; they MUST be returned with the remote error id and message.

REQ-SAG-0602 Quota exhaustion is not busy

Statements

  • A busy status whose body marks quota exhaustion MUST be returned at once as the error `http.quota_exhausted`.
  • A 429 with a body that does not mark quota exhaustion MUST be treated as busy.
  • A quota-exhausted response MUST NOT be resent.
